item.text: The bounded web pass is complete across all seven continuation chapters. I found recoverable new units for Taiwan coercion and crisis conduct, dissent and remedies, household/service exposure, elite appointments, and program-level implementation/adaptation; Chapter 7B remains the clearest shortfall because public evidence still does not establish Xi’s personal assets, enrichment, deception, or obstruction.

Research continuation completed for Chapters 2B–8B. No scores or rankings assigned.

Because the workspace is read-only, I could not physically update `research-ledger-manifest.json`; the following globally unique units are append-ready after `E048`.

### 2B — International peace, restraint, and lawful security

- `E049` — [CSIS ChinaPower, “2022 in ADIZ Violations”](https://chinapower.csis.org/analysis/2022-adiz-violations-china-dials-up-pressure-on-taiwan/), lines 95–105. In response to Pelosi’s August visit, PLA activity increased sharply: 446 aircraft operated in Taiwan’s ADIZ in August, 564 crossed the median line during 2022, and the exercises altered the prior operational status quo. Attribution is to Beijing/PLA policy and activity, not a proven personal Xi order. The source itself notes uncertainty about which PLA levels planned and executed the operations. Period fit: target year. Maps: `2B.2`, `2B.3`, `2B.10`.

- `E050` — [CSIS, “Speaker Pelosi’s Taiwan Visit”](https://www.csis.org/analysis/speaker-pelosis-taiwan-visit-implications-indo-pacific), lines 243–252. Beijing launched large-scale exercises, including missile activity, and suspended multiple U.S. dialogue channels. Beijing characterized the visit as the provocation; U.S. officials characterized the exercises as an overreaction. This preserves contrary interpretations rather than treating the event as uncontested aggression. Maps: `2B.1`, `2B.2`, `2B.7`, `2B.8`, `2B.10`.

- `E051` — [CSIS, “Alternatives to a Military Invasion of Taiwan”](https://www.csis.org/analysis/what-if-alternatives-chinese-military-invasion-taiwan), October 2022. The report analyzes coercive options short of invasion, including blockade and gray-zone pressure, as live strategic possibilities for Beijing. It is analytical rather than evidence of a specific 2022 decision, so attribution remains capability/posture-based. Maps: `2B.2`, `2B.3`, `2B.6`, `2B.10`.

- `E052` — [Axios, “U.S. warns China against a superpower proxy war in Ukraine”](https://www.axios.com/2022/03/15/china-ukraine-proxy-war-arm-russia), March 2022. U.S. officials warned that Chinese material support to Russia could create a proxy-war escalation, while public evidence did not establish that China transferred weapons. Xi’s pre-invasion alignment with Putin is relevant context; the article does not prove material support or personal authorization. Maps: `2B.5`, `2B.6`, `2B.9`.

Shortfall: no independently verified 2022 evidence of Chinese proxy operations, civilian-protection implementation, security-force accountability, or cross-border war initiation.

### 3B — Domestic safety and protection

- `E053` — [Freedom House China Media Bulletin](https://freedomhouse.org/report/china-media-bulletin/2022/grassroots-protests-xis-power-affirmed-us-midterms-disinformation), lines 94–119. The China Dissent Monitor recorded 668 mainland protest or dissent incidents from June–September 2022, including labor, property, COVID-access, and local-governance disputes. Freedom House recorded state violence in 60 incidents and detention/arrest in 48, while warning that this was likely an undercount. The same source documents citizens seeking redress, not merely political opposition. Maps: `3B.3`, `3B.5`, `3B.6`, `3B.9`, `3B.10`.

- `E054` — [World Bank China Economic Update, December 2022](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/china/publication/china-economic-update-december-2022), lines 45–51. The Bank identified limited hospital capacity, insufficient vulnerable-group vaccination, the need for effective treatments, unequal access to health and education, and youth unemployment. This is institutional assessment and exposure evidence, not proof of Xi-specific implementation failure. Maps: `3B.3`, `3B.8`, `3B.10`.

- `E055` — [Chinese mission response to the OHCHR Xinjiang assessment](https://www.ohchr.org/en/documents/country-reports/ohchr-assessment-human-rights-concerns-xinjiang-uyghur-autonomous-region), response materials associated with the 2022 assessment. Chinese authorities rejected the assessment as politically motivated and asserted that counterterrorism and deradicalization policies protected rights and prevented terrorism. This is contrary official evidence, retained as self-presentation without independent verification. Maps: `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.7`, `3B.9`.

Shortfall: no independent victim-level, court, medical, remedy, or subordinate-accountability record was located that materially resolves the attribution and correction gaps.

### 4B — Political freedom

- `E056` — [Freedom House China Media Bulletin](https://freedomhouse.org/report/china-media-bulletin/2022/grassroots-protests-xis-power-affirmed-us-midterms-disinformation), lines 96–115. The source documents pervasive surveillance, grid policing, new security laws, NGO closure, censorship, and widespread dissent despite those controls. It provides target-period evidence of both repression and continuing social challenge. Maps: `4B.2`, `4B.3`, `4B.4`, `4B.6`, `4B.9`, `4B.10`.

- `E057` — [Bloomberg, “How Xi’s Shakeup Shattered Decades of Succession Rules”](https://www.bloomberg.com/graphics/2022-china-party-congress-xi-new-leaders/), lines 177–200. The 2022 leadership lineup broke prior seniority and retirement conventions; Bloomberg reports that loyalty appeared central, Xi allies dominated the Standing Committee, and potential rivals were displaced. This supports appointment control and power concentration, but does not establish an unlawful process or personal motive. Maps: `4B.1`, `4B.5`, `4B.8`, `4B.10`.

- `E058` — [Freedom House, Freedom on the Net 2022](https://freedomhouse.org/country/china/freedom-net/2022). The report documents extensive online censorship, blocking of politically sensitive information, self-censorship, and narrow workarounds that still permitted some critical discussion. The existence of limited online criticism is contrary evidence against a claim of total information closure, while the broader environment remains highly restrictive. Maps: `4B.2`, `4B.3`, `4B.4`, `4B.7`, `4B.9`.

Shortfall: no credible evidence of competitive selection, independent institutional constraint, favorable corrective political action, or meaningful national-level accountability.

### 5B — Economic well-being

- `E059` — [World Bank China Economic Update, December 2022](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/china/publication/china-economic-update-december-2022), lines 42–51. The Bank projected 2.7% real growth in 2022, identified recurring COVID disruption and property-sector stress, and highlighted youth unemployment, regulatory predictability, social-security, health, and education gaps. Period fit is direct; attribution is to national policy conditions and shocks rather than Xi alone. Maps: `5B.1`, `5B.2`, `5B.3`, `5B.4`, `5B.6`, `5B.8`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`.

- `E060` — [IMF 2022 Article IV consultation](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2023/02/02/peoples-republic-of-china-2022-article-iv-consultation-press-release-staff-report-and-529067), lines 267–272. IMF reported expansionary macroeconomic policy in 2022 but also weak productivity, declining business dynamism, limited competitive neutrality between SOEs and private firms, and added burdens from strategic-sector assignments. Maps: `5B.3`, `5B.4`, `5B.5`, `5B.8`, `5B.10`.

- `E061` — [IMF Selected Issues for China](https://www.imf.org/-/media/Files/Publications/CR/2022/English/1CHNEA2022002.ashx), household-savings and distribution sections. The analysis links elevated precautionary savings to incomplete social protection, housing-related debt, job insecurity, and a widening urban–rural disposable-income gap. This is distributional and household evidence, but not a personal attribution finding. Maps: `5B.1`, `5B.2`, `5B.6`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`.

Shortfall: no defensible 2022 evidence of Xi-linked favoritism, appointment quality, household-level policy correction, or region-specific implementation outcomes.

### 6B — Social well-being

- `E062` — [World Bank China Economic Update, December 2022](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/china/publication/china-economic-update-december-2022), lines 45–50. The Bank recommended stronger vaccination of vulnerable groups, effective treatment access, better use of limited hospital capacity, increased social spending, and reduced inequality in healthcare and education. These recommendations identify service and equity gaps; they do not establish that all recommended measures failed. Maps: `6B.1`, `6B.3`, `6B.4`, `6B.6`, `6B.8`, `6B.9`, `6B.10`.

- `E063` — [Chinese government COVID measures for vulnerable groups](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/topnews/202212/27/content_WS63aae802c6d0a757729e4d37.html), 27 December 2022. Official measures prioritized vaccination in elderly-care and welfare institutions and boosters for people aged 60+, those with serious conditions, and immunocompromised groups. This is favorable protective-policy evidence, though implementation and coverage remain partly unverified. Maps: `6B.1`, `6B.3`, `6B.6`, `6B.8`.

- `E064` — [Time, “China’s Zero-COVID Trap”](https://time.com/6237990/china-end-zero-covid-policy/), 1 December 2022. Reporting described low elderly protection from vaccination, lower efficacy of domestic vaccines against severe disease, and insufficient healthcare capacity for reopening. It is adverse external reporting and includes model-based or comparative claims that require caution. Maps: `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.4`, `6B.6`, `6B.9`.

Shortfall: no robust 2022 household survey, regional service-quality audit, conditional-access record, or remedy evidence was located.

### 7B — Personal integrity and honesty

- `E065` — [Bloomberg leadership analysis](https://www.bloomberg.com/graphics/2022-china-party-congress-xi-new-leaders/), lines 180–200. The 2022 appointments concentrated power among officials with prior career overlap or loyalty ties to Xi, while established succession conventions were weakened. This supports a contested integrity-relevant appointment nexus, but does not prove dishonesty, enrichment, or corrupt intent. Maps: `7B.5`, `7B.9`.

- `E066` — [CCDI 2022 supervision and investigation statistics](https://www.ccdi.gov.cn/toutiaon/202301/t20230113_241506.html), 2022 national summary. The official disciplinary system reported nationwide supervision, investigations, and sanctions during 2022. This establishes institutional anti-corruption activity and accountability mechanisms, not Xi’s personal integrity or impartiality. Maps: `7B.6`, `7B.7`, `7B.10`.

Shortfall: targeted searches did not recover defensible evidence of Xi’s personal assets, enrichment, family benefit, deliberate falsehood, disclosure, correction, or obstruction. Closed-system silence remains non-probative.

### 8B — Effectiveness and competence

- `E067` — [IMF 2022 Article IV consultation](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2023/02/02/peoples-republic-of-china-2022-article-iv-consultation-press-release-staff-report-and-529067), lines 267–272. China demonstrated capacity for expansionary macroeconomic intervention, but IMF identified weak productivity, weak business dynamism, limited competitive neutrality, and structural burdens associated with state-owned enterprises and strategic-sector policy. Maps: `8B.2`, `8B.4`, `8B.6`, `8B.7`, `8B.10`.

- `E068` — [Reuters analysis of China’s COVID policy adjustments](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/analysis-china-makes-tweaks-but-tough-covid-policy-still-drags-on-economy-2847137), July 2022. China made incremental adjustments to zero-COVID controls but continued the overall policy while lagging in vaccination preparation needed for a safer exit. This supports implementation rigidity and delayed adaptation, while preserving the contrary fact that incremental adjustments occurred. Maps: `8B.1`, `8B.5`, `8B.7`, `8B.8`, `8B.10`.

- `E069` — [World Bank China Economic Update](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/china/publication/china-economic-update-december-2022), lines 42–51. The Bank identified both administrative capacity and clear implementation requirements: public-health adaptation, fiscal support, social spending, regulatory predictability, social-security reform, and youth-employment measures. The mixed assessment separates capacity from outcomes. Maps: `8B.1`, `8B.4`, `8B.5`, `8B.6`, `8B.7`, `8B.8`, `8B.10`.

- `E070` — [Chinese 2022 Government Work Report](https://www.china.org.cn/chinese/2022-03/14/content_78106770.htm), program and audit sections. The report set explicit implementation objectives for science and technology, rural development, low-carbon transition, public hospitals, local health capacity, and audit-based oversight. This is target-period program evidence and declared administrative reach, not outcome verification. Maps: `8B.1`, `8B.4`, `8B.5`, `8B.6`.

Shortfall: no independent program-level audit was found linking specific 2022 outcomes to Xi-owned programs, appointment decisions, or documented correction after failure.

### Disposition and accounting

- All units `E049–E070` are provisional accepted research units, subject to normal downstream deduplication.
- `E049` and `E050` describe overlapping Taiwan-crisis facts but retain distinct analytical roles: operational activity versus crisis interpretation and dialogue consequences.
- `E054`, `E059`, `E062`, and `E069` reuse the World Bank report for materially different claim units; they must not be counted as independent source families.
- `E057` and `E065` reuse Bloomberg for distinct political-freedom and integrity-nexus claims.
- Official Chinese protective or anti-corruption claims remain self-presentational unless independently corroborated.
- Missing evidence remains uncertainty, not negative evidence.
- No ledger manifest changes could be persisted because filesystem writes were unavailable.
